title: Typed Lifecycle Hooks

The bounded mutating delegation remained deterministically blocked by the stale promotion target (zetsu_agent_apply_target_not_clean); local implementation was used under the documented fallback, and the production control-plane checkout was not modified.

implementation.core_integration: LaplaceCore exposes one shared HookService and an owner-bound emit_hook adapter; the lifecycle surface is available without Zetsu.
semantics: Callbacks are registered Python callables with a typed HookContext and HookResult; no file discovery, plugin import, shell, subprocess or network hook path exists.
Matching callbacks execute sequentially in priority, registration-order and name order.
Events persist payload hash, stage and full owner/project/session/task identity under an idempotency key; duplicate replay returns without re-execution.
Security-sensitive PRE hooks fail closed on explicit block, exception, timeout or cancellation; the TASK_CANCEL cleanup stage still runs when its cancellation signal is already set.
POST hooks are constrained to observability-only policy: exceptions and timeouts are recorded and the operation continues; POST cancel results cannot block the operation.
Disabled hooks are skipped, scope filtering is owner/project-bound, and atomic state persistence supports restart/resume replay.

security_and_negative.bandit_note: Bandit returned zero high-severity findings; the hook engine has no subprocess, shell or dynamic code execution path.

ordering_and_failure_policy.ordering: priority ascending, then registration ordinal, then hook name
ordering_and_failure_policy.pre_security: HookFailurePolicy.FAIL_CLOSED for security-critical PRE stages; explicit block, exception, timeout and cancellation stop the operation.
ordering_and_failure_policy.post_observability: HookFailurePolicy.OBSERVE only; post exceptions/timeouts are attached to HookReport and do not block; post cancel is ignored for control flow.
ordering_and_failure_policy.cancellation: A cancellation signal stops cancellable stages before the next callback and is persisted; TASK_CANCEL hooks are allowed to run cleanup despite the signal.
ordering_and_failure_policy.idempotency: The first result is atomically persisted by idempotency_key. A same-identity replay returns replayed=true without invoking callbacks; payload, stage or identity conflicts fail closed.

comparison.method: The G9 frozen tests compare enabled/disabled paths, first dispatch/replay, security PRE failure, observability POST failure, cancellation and owner/project-scoped registrations. Correctness and security are preserved; no production model or hook performance claim was made.
comparison.reason: No hooks are registered by default and the typed service is shadowed until lifecycle callers opt in with explicit internal callbacks.

limitations: Existing retrieval, memory, mutation and verification call sites are not automatically instrumented; Core exposes the hook service for subsequent controlled integration.
A timed callback running in its own Python thread cannot be forcibly killed; the future is cancelled, the operation fails closed where required, and the bounded callback thread is allowed to unwind.
No model-token, latency, throughput or GPU measurement was performed for this lifecycle plumbing phase.
The full G0 certification was not repeated, per the roadmap instruction and prior phase certifications.
The socket-concurrency regression requires host socket permission because the restricted shell denies socket creation; the selected unchanged suite passed under that permission.
